executionResult.executionNotes: Continuous view now virtualizes large documents with five page nodes/canvases and proportional spacers; thumbnail source and render-state caches are evicted outside the visible virtualized window, and off-window renders are discarded. A 5,000-page structural resource test verifies the bounds, page-window navigation, and thumbnail cache eviction. Existing autosave/crash-recovery workflow tests also pass. During packaged-viewer validation, fixed a PDF.js buffer-ownership regression by passing copies to render and text-extraction workers; this prevents preview work from detaching the retained document bytes used by form parsing. Focused regression tests pass, and the packaged viewer opens the sample document with page previews and no user-facing errors. This is structural resource profiling, not a real-world heap or latency benchmark.

verification.summary: The focused PDF workspace suite passed all 53 tests. The full Angular suite passed all 126 tests with 78.39% statement, 83.50% line, and 86.66% function coverage (branch coverage 58.28%). The focused PDF render service suite passed all four tests, including checks that PDF.js receives cloned bytes and leaves the source buffer intact. All four extension tests passed. The Chrome ZIP and Firefox XPI rebuilt successfully, and packaged-viewer validation confirmed the sample PDF rendered with page previews and no user-facing errors. Large-document tests verified a five-page continuous render window and thumbnail caches constrained to the visible window; autosave recovery coverage passed.

executionResult.executionNotes: Added ZIP/XPI archive generation, store listing/privacy metadata, and submission instructions. Chrome/Edge ZIP and Firefox XPI bundles were built; required manifest, background, popup, viewer, and icon files were verified, and all four extension tests passed. With user approval, generated neutral draft branding plus two genuine screenshots of the packaged Chrome viewer using the local two-page demo PDF; the listing records those images as captured and publisher-review-required. The packages remain unsigned and the artwork is not publisher-approved. Store signing and publisher review still require the publisher's accounts, so this task remains blocked.
